learning_outcomes.text: Promote the development of personality in all its dimensions: scientific, cultural, human, etc.; so that it results in a greater development of critical capacity and a knowledge of problems, leading to an exercise of freedom that, respecting legitimate pluralism, is sensitive to manifestations of solidarity and fraternity and helps to build spaces of equality, coexistence and friendship.
Promote the social values proper to a peaceful culture, contributing to democratic coexistence, respect for Human Rights and fundamental principles such as equality and non-discrimination.
Understand that it is characteristic of the university spirit to critically and reflectively approach the study of one's own discipline in its connection with other fields of knowledge.
Identify the most relevant questions of human existence present in great religious, humanistic, and scientific creations and adopt a reasoned personal stance towards them.
Discover and evaluate the anthropological assumptions and ethical repercussions of one's own discipline.

teaching_methods: reading of classic and contemporary texts on the foundations of ethics
classroom discussion activities based on real cases
essay writing based on a selected book
extracurricular seminars on book readings to foster critical thinking
assessment_rules: There will be a single written exam, which will take place on the last day of class. This exam will count for 100% of the course grade. The essay on a book proposed by the professor is an extra 10%. The extraordinary resit exam will be similar to the ordinary exam.
